questions: Does it affect the tool behaviour?
Does it affect the guide's accuracy?
Does it affect the answerability of tasks?
Does it affect the expected answers?
procedure: Classify each difference first, against the five questions.
Record it in the preflight record, with its evidence.
Fix any affected setup: the tool configuration, the guide (through its independent check, decision J), the reference solutions or the answer key.
Run the relevant Direct Access and Guided Direct Access smoke checks again.
An unexplained discrepancy blocks the freeze. It is not carried into scored execution.

decisionL.judgement: The backend preflight holds for the real Missions backend: every real soak and outage passed on all five scenarios; the one host-free-min failure is the simulated alpha soak under host-application memory pressure, not the stack; decision L found no unexplained discrepancy. Answerability (step 7) and the paid smoke test (step 9) remain for later Jobs.
decisionL.judgedBy: the lead developer, choosing the worker's proposed wording in the worker session on 2026-11-01 (UTC)

A.text: serialization: server, content-length and transfer-encoding headers, and body bytes; the six list pages are equal as parsed XML

B.text: illustrative error message text in the body; the error codes are equal

C.text: HEAD and unknown paths: the real service answers 405 with Allow (or 404), the simulator 501 html; documented in study/preflight/README.md

D.text: features the simulator lacks: /missions/{id}/changes, the ETag, the status filter check, the Accept check and the trailing-slash rule; the real service's answers agree with study 1's frozen guide (study/guide/enterprise-legacy-systems-guide.md) where that guide specifies the behaviour

E.text: latency, not a probe difference: Missions REST median 17 ms real against 4 ms simulated in step 4; the router full page median about 0.44 s on real in every block

decisionL.classification: Proposed by the worker and accepted by the lead developer as proposed on 2026-11-01 (UTC): the responses differ in every group. The differences include tool-visible response changes (status, content type, body) and transport headers that the raw tools do not return (server, content-length, transfer-encoding, allow, etag); toolVisible marks which. No corrective setup change was identified for scored runs, which use the real Missions backend: no change to the tool configuration, the guide, the reference solutions or the answer key. Guide accuracy and answerability stay pending their own checks (the guide's check under decision J, and step 7). Group D is a simulator gap, recorded as unfit for those paths, not a defect of the real service. Every difference has a known cause, so decision L does not block the freeze.
